activities.anchor: so libraries are warehouses for what a search box already delivers
activities.caption: find the line the everything-is-online myth would love
activities.name: flsOnlineSpot

config.prompt: One line of this summary is the search-box myth speaking — click it:
lines: Most of the recorded past is not digitised — archives, deep back-runs of journals, government documents, most books out of commercial print.
What is online arrives ranked by advertising economics rather than selected and catalogued against standards.
The library's scarce goods — trustworthiness, durability, free access at the point of use — are precisely the ones the open web does not supply.
Most books out of commercial print are already digitised and available free online.
The digitisation era expanded the profession rather than retiring it.
config.correction: Most books out of commercial print are NOT digitised — that absence is a large part of the library's continuing job.
config.why: Archives, journal back-runs, government documents and out-of-print books are the deep record — the reason the digitisation era expanded the profession instead of retiring it.

activities.anchor: founded in the third century BCE
activities.caption: scrub the institution's long arc
activities.name: flsHistoryTimeline

events.title: The Library of Alexandria
events.text: To collect a copy of every work in the known world, in Greek and in translation — the first systematic bibliographies, and Homer's epics divided into the standard books still used.

events.title: Caesar's blaze
events.text: Part of the collection, stored near the harbour, burns — damage, not the single cataclysm of legend.

events.title: University libraries grow
events.text: Alongside European universities from the 1100s; monasteries had copied manuscripts through long ages of rare literacy.

events.title: Dewey and the ALA
events.text: Melvil Dewey publishes the decimal classification; the American Library Association is founded — the profession's twin halves born together.

events.title: Ranganathan's five laws
events.text: Books are for use; every reader his book; every book its reader; save the time of the reader; a library is a growing organism.

events.title: The Library Bill of Rights
events.text: Materials for the interest, information and enlightenment of all people; challenge censorship; deny no one service.

activities.anchor: was destroyed in a single cataclysmic fire
activities.caption: bet on how Alexandria actually ended
activities.name: flsAlexandriaPredict

config.q: The Library of Alexandria: how did it actually end?
choices: Caesar's 48 BCE blaze levelled the whole thing in one afternoon
A long decline: partial damage in 48 BCE, then funding cuts and political instability — faded from function by late antiquity
The caliph's army burned it in the seventh century
config.why: No single villain, no dramatic ending — the caliph story is a much later legend. The field's quieter, sharper lesson: collections die of neglect, not catastrophe, which is why preservation is a budget line, not an act of heroism.

activities.anchor: on the principle that a man who dies rich dies disgraced
activities.caption: call the Carnegie building count
activities.name: flsCarnegieEstimate

config.prompt: How many library buildings did Andrew Carnegie alone fund worldwide?
config.why: More than 2,500 buildings worldwide, roughly 1,700 of them in the United States — the same access for the poor as for the rich. And in 1876 the profession's twin foundations were laid: Dewey's decimal classification and the American Library Association.
config.context: The free public library — taxation-funded, open to every resident — spread on the argument that access to knowledge is a public good, like clean water.

activities.anchor: compressed the mission into five laws in 1931
activities.caption: line up the five laws as the manifesto reads
activities.name: flsLawsOrder

config.prompt: Ranganathan's manifesto, in the canonical order:
items: Save the time of the reader.
A library is a growing organism.
config.why: The mission compressed in 1931 still reads as one — and none of the laws mentions a format, which is why they have aged so well.

activities.anchor: the org chart is the life cycle
activities.caption: fill the pipeline's station names
activities.name: flsCycleCloze

config.text: Information is %%created%% (an author writes, a government publishes, a scientist reports), %%disseminated%% (through publishers, vendors, databases), selected and organised (acquisitions chooses; cataloguing describes), %%preserved%% (conservation, digitisation, format migration), and finally used (circulation lends, reference connects, instruction teaches).
config.hint: Three of the five stations, in order — author to shelf to future.

activities.anchor: The organisation stage deserves a closer look
activities.caption: pair each tool with the job it does
activities.name: flsToolsMatch

config.prompt: The core technology — pair each tool with its job:

pairs.right: ten top-level classes subdivided by subject — 510 shelved beside 510 in any Dewey library on Earth
finer subject divisions for research collections
standardised records of author, title, edition, publisher, subject headings — increasingly linked data
records exchanged between libraries — the ancestor of WorldCat's shared holdings

config.why: The engineering problem: describe an item so that a person who has never seen it, and did not create it, can find it among millions.

activities.anchor: distinguished by whom they serve and how they are funded
activities.caption: file each trait by its library family
activities.name: flsFamilyBuckets

config.prompt: One science, many missions — file each trait by its family:

items.label: local taxation and boards — accountable to (and vulnerable to) local politics
internet access, job-search help, children's programming — the social safety net
deep subject collections, expensive journal subscriptions, liaison librarians
information literacy as an accredited learning outcome
law firm and hospital knowledge services
one organisation's precise needs, one funder

config.why: Around the family stand the national libraries with legal deposit — a copy of everything published in the country — plus archives and museums sharing standards and staff. What unites them: the same selection, description, preservation and ethics; only the community changes.
